--- title: "For the same IKEA furniture, Estonia runs low and Ireland high" subtitle: "Across 34 identical IKEA articles sold in all 16 euro markets, Estonia's pre-VAT price falls below each article's market median on 31 of 34; Ireland's rises above it on 29. Between them, Germany splits 17–17." description: "A dot plot comparing the pre-VAT prices of 34 identical IKEA articles across all 16 euro markets shows Estonia consistently low and Ireland consistently high, while mid-table markets like Germany split evenly. Prices are VAT-adjusted and indexed to each article's own median, removing currency and tax effects. Built in R with ggplot2, ggtext and showtext." date: "2026-10-26" author: - name: "Steven Ponce" url: "https://stevenponce.netlify.app" citation: url: "https://stevenponce.netlify.app/data_visualizations/TidyTuesday/2026/tt_2026_43.html" categories: ["TidyTuesday", "2026"] tags: [ "IKEA", "Retail Pricing", "Price Comparison", "Eurozone", "VAT Adjustment", "Dot Plot", "Strip Plot", "Distribution", "Log Scale", "Robustness Checks", "ggtext", "showtext", "ggplot2", "2026" ] image: "thumbnails/tt_2026_43.png" format: html: toc: true toc-depth: 5 code-link: true code-fold: true code-tools: true code-summary: "Show code" editor_options: chunk_output_type: inline execute: freeze: true cache: true error: false message: false warning: false eval: true --- ![Strip plot titled "For the same IKEA furniture, Estonia runs low and Ireland high." Sixteen euro markets are stacked as rows, and each row has 34 grey dots, one per identical IKEA article, placed by its pre-VAT price relative to that article's median across the 16 markets, on a log scale from minus 30 to plus 50 percent. A burgundy tick marks each market's median. Estonia sits lowest: below the article median on 31 of 34 articles, with a median about 12 percent under. Ireland and Finland sit highest, about 12 percent over; Ireland is above on 29 of 34. Mid-table markets such as Germany split 17 below and 17 above. A right-hand column lists below, tie, and above counts for every market. A note explains that the three Baltic markets share a shelf price on 31 of 34 articles, so Estonia's higher VAT leaves it with a lower pre-VAT price. Data: IKEA.com listings on 28 September 2026, via TidyTuesday.](tt_2026_43.png){#fig-1} ### [**Steps to Create this Graphic**]{.mark} #### [1. Load Packages & Setup]{.smallcaps} ::: {.cell} ````{.cell-code} ```{{r}} #| label: load #| warning: false #| message: false #| results: "hide" ## 1. LOAD PACKAGES & SETUP ---- suppressPackageStartupMessages({ if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman") pacman::p_load( tidyverse, ggtext, showtext, janitor, scales, glue, ggview, magick ) }) # Source utility functions suppressMessages(source(here::here("R/utils/fonts.R"))) source(here::here("R/utils/social_icons.R")) source(here::here("R/utils/image_utils.R")) source(here::here("R/themes/base_theme.R")) ``` ```` ::: #### [2. Read in the Data]{.smallcaps} ::: {.cell} ````{.cell-code} ```{{r}} #| label: read #| include: true #| eval: true #| warning: false ### |- figure settings ---- fig_w <- 10 fig_h <- 8 fig_dpi <- 320 out_file <- "2026/Week_43/2026_43.png" setup_fonts() fonts <- get_font_families() ## 2. READ IN THE DATA ---- tt <- tidytuesdayR::tt_load(2026, week = 43) ikea_seating_raw <- tt$ikea_seating |> clean_names() rm(tt) ``` ```` ::: #### [3. Examine the Data]{.smallcaps} ::: {.cell} ````{.cell-code} ```{{r}} #| label: examine #| include: true #| eval: true #| results: 'hide' #| warning: false ## 3. EXAMINING THE DATA ---- glimpse(ikea_seating_raw) skimr::skim(ikea_seating_raw) ``` ```` ::: #### [4. Tidy Data]{.smallcaps} ::: {.cell} ````{.cell-code} ```{{r}} #| label: tidy #| warning: false ### |- 2026 standard VAT rates, euro markets ---- vat_rates <- c( at = 0.20, be = 0.21, de = 0.19, ee = 0.24, es = 0.21, fi = 0.255, fr = 0.20, hr = 0.25, ie = 0.23, it = 0.22, lt = 0.21, lv = 0.21, nl = 0.21, pt = 0.23, si = 0.22, sk = 0.23 ) market_names <- c( at = "Austria", be = "Belgium", de = "Germany", ee = "Estonia", es = "Spain", fi = "Finland", fr = "France", hr = "Croatia", ie = "Ireland", it = "Italy", lt = "Lithuania", lv = "Latvia", nl = "Netherlands", pt = "Portugal", si = "Slovenia", sk = "Slovakia" ) ### |- euro listings, one row per market x article ---- euro <- ikea_seating_raw |> filter(currency == "EUR") |> distinct(country, item_no, .keep_all = TRUE) |> mutate(price_net = price / (1 + unname(vat_rates[country]))) ### |- fixed cohort: articles listed in all 16 euro markets ---- cohort <- euro |> add_count(item_no, name = "n_markets") |> filter(n_markets == 16) |> mutate( article_median = median(price_net), rel_price = price_net / article_median, side = case_when( price_net < article_median - 0.005 ~ "below", price_net > article_median + 0.005 ~ "above", TRUE ~ "tie" ), .by = item_no ) ### |- per-market summary ---- market_summary <- cohort |> summarise( median_rel = median(rel_price), below = sum(side == "below"), tie = sum(side == "tie"), above = sum(side == "above"), .by = country ) |> mutate(market = unname(market_names[country])) |> arrange(median_rel) market_levels <- market_summary$market # cheapest at the bottom cohort <- cohort |> mutate(market = factor(unname(market_names[country]), levels = market_levels)) market_summary <- market_summary |> mutate( market = factor(market, levels = market_levels), named = country %in% c("ee", "ie", "de") ) ### |- counts quoted in the copy ---- n_ee_below <- market_summary$below[market_summary$country == "ee"] n_ie_above <- market_summary$above[market_summary$country == "ie"] n_de_below <- market_summary$below[market_summary$country == "de"] n_de_above <- market_summary$above[market_summary$country == "de"] # Baltic markets: shared shelf price (with VAT), different VAT baltic_prices <- cohort |> filter(country %in% c("ee", "lv", "lt")) |> select(item_no, country, price) |> pivot_wider(names_from = country, values_from = price) n_baltic_same <- sum(baltic_prices$ee == baltic_prices$lv & baltic_prices$lv == baltic_prices$lt) n_lv_lt_same <- sum(baltic_prices$lv == baltic_prices$lt) ### |- count-column layout (secondary to the dots) ---- count_cols <- tibble( side = c("below", "tie", "above"), x = c(1.74, 1.88, 2.02) ) count_labels <- market_summary |> select(market, named, below, tie, above) |> pivot_longer(c(below, tie, above), names_to = "side", values_to = "n") |> left_join(count_cols, by = "side") ``` ```` ::: #### [5. Visualization Parameters]{.smallcaps} ::: {.cell} ````{.cell-code} ```{{r}} #| label: params #| include: true #| warning: false ### |- plot aesthetics ---- clrs <- get_theme_colors( palette = list( dot = "#2C2825", median = "#722F37", ref = "#B9B1A6", muted = "#7A7068", ink = "#2C2825" ) ) ### |- titles and caption ---- title_text <- "For the same IKEA furniture, Estonia runs low and Ireland high" subtitle_text <- str_glue( "Across 34 identical IKEA articles sold in all 16 euro markets, Estonia's pre-VAT price falls below each
", "article's market median on **{n_ee_below} of 34**; Ireland's rises above it on **{n_ie_above}**. ", "Between them, Germany splits **{n_de_below}–{n_de_above}**.

", "Each dot is one article's price before VAT, relative to that article's ", "median across the 16 markets." ) annotation_text <- str_glue( "The three Baltic markets share a shelf price on {n_baltic_same} of 34 articles ", "(Latvia and Lithuania on all {n_lv_lt_same}). Estonia's higher VAT (24% versus 21%) ", "leaves it with a lower pre-VAT price." ) disclosure_text <- paste0( "Snapshot of ikea.com listings on 28 Sep 2026. Pre-VAT price = shelf price ÷ (1 + 2026 standard VAT rate).
", "VAT rates: VATupdate. Log scale: +25% and −20% sit the same distance from the median.
", "Tie = price equal to the article's median. The 34 articles include one children's armchair frame." ) caption_text <- paste0( disclosure_text, "
", create_social_caption( tt_year = 2026, tt_week = 43, source_text = "ikea.com via TidyTuesday (curated by Georgios Karamanis)" ) ) ### |- plot theme ---- base_theme <- create_base_theme(clrs) weekly_theme <- extend_weekly_theme( base_theme, theme( plot.title = element_text( face = "bold", family = fonts$title_1, size = 24, color = "#2C2825", margin = margin(b = 8) ), plot.subtitle = element_markdown( family = fonts$subtitle, size = 11.5, color = "#2C2825", lineheight = 1.25, margin = margin(b = 14) ), plot.caption = element_markdown( family = fonts$caption, size = 7, color = "#7A7068", hjust = 0, lineheight = 1.3, margin = margin(t = 14) ), plot.title.position = "plot", plot.caption.position = "plot", axis.text.y = element_text(family = fonts$text, size = 10.5, color = "#2C2825", hjust = 1), axis.text.x = element_text(family = fonts$text, size = 9, color = "#7A7068"), axis.title = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "gray90", linewidth = 0.3), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "none", plot.margin = margin(20, 24, 14, 20) ) ) theme_set(weekly_theme) ``` ```` ::: #### [6. Plot]{.smallcaps} ::: {.cell} ````{.cell-code} ```{{r}} #| label: plot #| warning: false ### |- main plot ---- ### |- axis: percent from the article median, on a log scale ---- x_breaks <- c(0.7, 0.8, 0.9, 1, 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5) x_labels <- c("−30%", "−20%", "−10%", "median", "+10%", "+20%", "+30%", "+40%", "+50%") p <- ggplot(cohort, aes(x = rel_price, y = market)) + # reference line at the article median geom_vline(xintercept = 1, color = "#B9B1A6", linewidth = 0.5) + # one dot per article geom_point( position = position_jitter(height = 0.18, width = 0, seed = 43), color = "#2C2825", alpha = 0.42, size = 1.7, stroke = 0 ) + # market median tick geom_segment( data = market_summary, aes( x = median_rel, xend = median_rel, y = as.integer(market) - 0.34, yend = as.integer(market) + 0.34 ), color = "#722F37", linewidth = 1.3, lineend = "butt" ) + # direct label for the median tick, on the top row only annotate( "text", x = market_summary$median_rel[market_summary$market == last(market_levels)], y = length(market_levels) + 0.55, label = "market median", family = fonts$text, size = 2.8, color = "#722F37", hjust = 0.5 ) + # count column, secondary: grey, small, named markets in ink geom_text( data = count_labels, aes(x = x, y = market, label = n, color = named), family = fonts$text, size = 3.1, hjust = 0.5 ) + annotate( "text", x = count_cols$x, y = length(market_levels) + 0.85, label = count_cols$side, family = fonts$text, size = 2.8, color = "#7A7068", hjust = 0.5 ) + annotate( "text", x = mean(count_cols$x), y = length(market_levels) + 1.45, label = "articles of 34", family = fonts$text, size = 2.8, color = "#7A7068", fontface = "bold", hjust = 0.5 ) + # Estonia-Latvia annotation, in the empty right side of the Baltic rows annotate( "text", x = 1.12, y = 2, label = str_wrap(annotation_text, 46), # 46 keeps "24% versus 21%" on one line, no orphan family = fonts$text, size = 3, color = "#7A7068", hjust = 0, vjust = 0.5, lineheight = 1.1 ) + scale_color_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#2C2825", `FALSE` = "#7A7068"), guide = "none") + scale_x_log10( breaks = x_breaks, labels = x_labels, limits = c(0.66, 2.1), expand = expansion(0) ) + scale_y_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(0.6, 1.9))) + labs( title = title_text, subtitle = subtitle_text, caption = caption_text ) ``` ```` ::: ### [7. Save]{.smallcaps} ::: {.cell} ````{.cell-code} ```{{r}} #| label: save #| warning: false ### |- save ---- main_path <- here::here("data_visualizations", "TidyTuesday", "2026", "tt_2026_43.png") thumb_path <- here::here("data_visualizations", "TidyTuesday", "2026", "thumbnails", "tt_2026_43.png") # Full-size version, for the QMD figure ggview::save_ggplot(plot = p, file = main_path, width = fig_w, height = fig_h, units = "in", dpi = fig_dpi) # Reduced-size thumbnail, for the YAML `image:` field fs::dir_create(dirname(thumb_path)) magick::image_read(main_path) |> magick::image_resize("400") |> magick::image_write(thumb_path) ``` ```` ::: #### [8.
